items.title: 床置きローアングルも膝猫自撮りも自由自在！ 折りたたみスマホが猫撮影に革命を起こしてきた歴史
items.summary: Apple初の折りたたみスマホ「iPhone Duo」登場を記念し、折りたたみ端末の魅力を「猫撮影」から紐解くコラムです。歴代GALAXY Z Foldなどで実践してきた半開きでのローアングル撮影やアウトカメラ自撮りの便利さを解説。約36万円の新モデルがスマホ界に開く新たな扉への期待を語ります
items.titleJa: 床置きローアングルも膝猫自撮りも自由自在！ 折りたたみスマホが猫撮影に革命を起こしてきた歴史

items.titleJa: MCP サーバーと繋いだだけで情報漏洩？ 危険の4パターンと事前に確認すべき7つのことをまとめてみた
items.summaryJa: MCPサーバーをAIエージェントに追加すると、ツールの呼び出し先をAIが決定する一方で、間違った設定や外部の書き込みを読むことによる乗っ取りの危険があると整理されています。事例と調査から、ツールポイズニング・間接プロンプトインジェクション・長期有効キー・自動承認の4パターンが挙げられ、それぞれ対策として最小権限や人の確認を組み合わせるべきだと指摘されています。追加前には提供元・最新性の確認、外部書き込みの扱い、スコープ、権限、キーの管理、承認設定など7つのチェック項目を必ず確認することが推奨されています。

items.title: 「暗すぎる」を CIELAB ΔE で測ったら、原因は明度ではなかった
items.summary: Three.js の低ポリシーンで、Night パレットが3本のプロトタイプを通して「暗すぎる」と診断され続け、明度を上げても直りませんでした。CIELAB ΔE で測ったら原因は明度ではなく色どうしの距離で、3つに分解できました。この記事は、測定の実装（TypeScript 約30行）、4パレットの実測値、閾値をテストに落とす書き方、そして測ったのに誤診した失敗を書きます。 前提 作っているのは、オレンジの球が小さな世界を旅するポートフォリオサイトです。 Three.js 0.184 / React Three Fiber 9 / TypeScript 5.7 / Vitest ...
items.titleJa: 「暗すぎる」を CIELAB ΔE で測ったら、原因は明度ではなかった
items.summaryJa: 本記事は、Three.js の低ポリシーンで「暗すぎる」と診断されたNight系パレットの原因を、明度ではなく色の距離（CIELAB ΔE）で分析した経緯を記録している。測定実装を含む4パレットの実測値と、閾値をテストに落とす方法、誤診の経験談を詳述し、DeltaEを用いて3つの要因（建物の色の組み合わせ、地面/パッチ、屋根/空）の影響を分解した。結論として、Nightの問題は色の距離によるもので、Goldenは別の問題で球体/空が最悪値となっていた。

items.titleJa: OpenAI、「GPT-6 Sol」「GPT-6 Luna」を発表 ——速度と費用効率を重視、API入出力単価はGPT-5.6版比でSolが半額、Lunaが半額以下に

items.title: 12 CSS features that can retire your dependencies
items.summary: 🚀 Frontend Focus #​759 — September 23, 2026 | Read on the web 🧭 WebKit Features for Safari 27.0 — An epic set of release notes covers Safari 27's enhancements, including its new MCP server (let agents debug your work), scroll anchoring , the customizable element, a controls attribute for images in visionOS, sizes="auto" for images, and more. WebKit 💡 In related news, Xcode 27.1 Beta includes an iPhone Duo simulator if you want to see how things look on Apple's forthcoming foldable. Skeleton Loaders Are Just Slow Queries in Disguise — You add a skeleton loader to hide the wait. But that wait is a slow query, and it only grows with your data. TimescaleDB extends Postgres so the data behind your components returns fast at scale, no matter how big it gets. Get $1000 credit to start . Tiger Data (creators of TimescaleDB) sponsor 12 CSS Features You Can Use Today with No Build Step — Highlights various CSS features that we can turn to now , retiring some toolchain dependencies in turn. Things like native nesting instead of Sass, :has() instead of wrapper-class hacks, and more. Flavio Copes Blurry Before Beautiful: Image Previews for the Web? — Having a 'blurry' version of an image load in before the full version isn't new, but the Edge team is proposing a previewsrc attribute so browsers can handle it natively. Patrick Brosset (Microsoft) ⚡️ IN BRIEF 🛠️ Chrome's latest DevTools update brings DevTools MCP server improvements, ad script tracking, more modern devices in Device Mode, and more. 🌏 A recent Edge update adds the OpaqueRange API for text-range UIs, component accessibility improvements, and the agent-ready WebMCP API. ☑️ Chrome 155 beta adds support for the CSS symbols() function, margin-trim , JPEG XL images, and more. 📙 Articles, Opinions & Tutorials The Root Scroller and How Not to Lose It — The ‘root scroller’ is the viewport’s scroll container and handles things like scroll restoration and collapsing mobile address bars. But common CSS patterns can hand scrolling to other elements and lose those features, as shown in this demo-packed explainer. Kilian Valkhof "AI, Make the Website Good" — Zach argues that, no matter the tools, caring about the quality of output matters more than ever. He amusingly illustrates this point by highlighting the front of house output of top AI companies. Zach Leatherman The Era of Agentic Mobile Development Is Built on Expo — Build with our CLI and dev tools. Test on our cloud simulators. And ship with the best CI/CD for mobile development. Expo sponsor 19½ Things You Didn't Know About Accessibility in HTML and CSS — A neat slide-driven writeup of a StripeCon Europe talk rounds up lesser-known accessibility details. Manuel Matuzovic 'CSS Scroll-Triggered Animations Are Here, And I Completely Missed Them' — Scroll- triggered animations shipped in Chrome back in February. Cyd catches us up on how they differ from regular and scroll-driven animations, and looks at the timeline-trigger and animation-trigger properties specifically. Cyd Stumpel Responsive iframes in Chrome 154 — Landed in Chrome, and in preview in Edge, responsively-sized iframes are now a thing. You can set an iframe to be the size of its content, set which dimension that size is derived from, and tweak dynamically. The only catch is the embedded document must opt in. Sebastian Benz & Bramus van Damme A Decent Custom Checkbox Pattern for Until ::checkmark is Ready — Until ::checkmark reaches checkboxes, Andy lays a transparent native input over a custom box with an SVG tick. Andy Bell We Found a Fix for 'Wobbly Spinners' in Safari — CSS’s round() function came to the rescue here. Cody Olsen The Death of Web Development Education: Rescuing a Field From Disappearing Mathias Schäfer 🧰 Tools, Code & Resources Critical 9.0: Extract and Inline Critical Path CSS in HTML — A total rewrite of the popular critical CSS inliner, used to improve first render and LCP. Version 9 picks between two engines: a fast, browser-free one for prerendered HTML and a Playwright-based one for SPAs. Plus MCP support. Addy Osmani and Ben Zörb 📊 Plotly.js 4: A Major Update for the Popular Charting Library — It adds ‘quiver’ plots for drawing vector fields (with many fantastic examples in the post), accepts any CSS Color 4 color string, and removes the use of Mapbox GL in favor of MapLibre. Chris Parmer Build Forms That Fit Your Frontend—and Any Backend — Create custom themes for your form UI or use style adapters for Bootstrap, MUI, and Shadcn/UI. Dedicated npm packages for React, Angular, and Vue. SurveyJS sponsor Semfont: A Font That Reads What You Wrote — A small library that auto-styles text word-by-word, scoring each word (by sentiment, salience, and more) and then applying color, weight, and slant. items.title: GPT-6 Sol and Luna now available on AI Gateway
items.summary: GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna from OpenAI are now available on AI Gateway . Both models bring GPT-6 improvements in professional work, coding, computer use, factuality, and communication at a lower price than GPT-6 Astra . GPT-6 Sol ( openai/gpt-6-sol ) is suited to complex professional workflows and sustained coding tasks where quality and room to iterate both matter. GPT-6 Luna ( openai/gpt-6-luna ) is the lower-cost option for high-volume agentic workflows, coding, and everyday tasks. Both Sol and Luna communicate more directly than their GPT-5.6 counterparts, with less jargon and fewer low-value details. They also improve factual reliability and are less likely to make misleading claims about work completed during coding tasks. Use openai/gpt-6-sol and openai/gpt-6-luna across the AI SDK , OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API , OpenAI-compatible Responses API , and coding agents connected to AI Gateway. Install the latest Vercel CLI and connect your supported coding agents to AI Gateway: Then select openai/gpt-6-sol for longer or more demanding coding work, or openai/gpt-6-luna when throughput is the priority. AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage, and configuring retries, failover, and routing. Try GPT-6 Sol or GPT-6 Luna in the model playground, or view all language models available on AI Gateway. Read more

items.title: Claude Opus 5.5 now available on AI Gateway
items.summary: Claude Opus 5.5 from Anthropic is now available on AI Gateway . It is a step-change improvement over Opus 5 , with its biggest gains in agentic coding, long-running agent tasks, and knowledge work. Anthropic cites that Opus 5.5 performs at the level of Fable 5.1, but ~30% faster and ~40% cheaper than Opus 5 per task. Opus 5.5 is also a better collaborator over long runs. It reports back in plain language on what it did, what it found, and what it needs next, making it easier to supervise work that spans many steps or takes place over a longer period. Opus 5.5 includes two API changes that can turn previously valid requests into HTTP 400 errors: Thinking is always adaptive. Requests that disable thinking or set a fixed thinking budget are rejected. The model decides how much to think for each request. Use effort and prompting to steer its thinking behavior. Forced tool use is retired. Requests cannot require a tool call or force a specific tool. Prompt the model toward the tool, then catch and retry misses in your harness. If you previously forced a tool call to return JSON, use structured outputs instead. Use anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 across the AI SDK , OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API , Anthropic Messages API , and coding agents connected to AI Gateway. You can also enable fast mode with the gateway speed option r anthropic/claude-opus-5.5-fast . The model has a 1M-token context window, returns up to 128K tokens, and has a June 2026 knowledge cutoff. Regional inference and Zero Data Retention Regional inference and Zero Data Retention are opt-in request controls. This example pins inference to the US and ZDR: Use Opus 5.5 in coding agents Install the latest Vercel CLI and connect your supported coding agents to AI Gateway: Then select anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 in the agent. In Claude Code , use /fast to toggle fast mode for the session. See the coding agents guide for other agent-specific instructions. AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. Try Claude Opus 5.5 in the model playground , or view all language models available on AI Gateway. Read more

items.title: AI Gateway now supports TypeSafe clients and an HTTP API for Jev
items.summary: You can now call Jev from TypeSafe AI through AI Gateway using an existing TypeSafe client or the HTTP API, in addition to the AI SDK. TypeSafe client: Point an existing TypeSafe client at AI Gateway without changing its evaluation calls. HTTP API: Call Jev directly from any language or framework. AI SDK: Call Jev from a TypeScript application using AI SDK. Jev is a probabilistic decision model for software. State goes in, and typed answers come out with probabilities attached, so there's no generated text to parse. Requests are billed through AI Gateway on all three paths, so they appear alongside your other model calls in usage and observability. Migrate an existing TypeSafe client Change the base URL and API key. Your systemOne calls, noul questions, and response shapes stay exactly as they are. Start a new integration New integrations name the model as typesafe-ai/jev and ask one of three question types: boolean returns a probability from 0 to 1, choice picks one option from a set you name, and score rates against a scale you define. This example asks whether an agent should keep working after fixing a bug and passing its tests. With the HTTP API, POST to /v1/evaluate : With the AI SDK, run the same evaluation through evaluate : You can also use Jev through eve , a framework for building and deploying agents with sandboxed compute, human approvals, and evaluations already built in. eve uses Jev as the default evaluation model for automatic model selection, typed evaluations, and automated tool approvals. See the TypeSafe-compatible API guide to migrate a client, or the evaluation guide for the HTTP API or AI SDK . Read more

items.title: Googleの「Gemini」も能力テスト中に実在企業3社に侵入──WSJ報道

items.title: UI制御だけでは担保できない冪等性。ブラウザ仕様から考察するフロントエンド設計
items.summary: はじめに：フロントエンドにおける冪等性の落とし穴 Webアプリケーションにおいて、データの整合性を守るための冪等性（Idempotency）の担保は重要です。 特に決済処理やデータ更新などでは、APIの多重リクエストを防ぐために、ボタン押下時にHTMLの disabled 属性を付与したり、ローディングオーバーレイでガードをかけるのが一般的なプラクティスです。 しかし実務において、これらのUIによるガードをすり抜け、APIが複数回発火してしまうケースに直面しました。 具体的には、1フレーム未満（十数ミリ秒程度）の間隔で連続入力（マウスのチャタリングを想定）が発生した場合、ローディング...
items.titleJa: UI制御だけでは担保できない冪等性。ブラウザ仕様から考察するフロントエンド設計
items.summaryJa: UIガードだけでは冪等性を完全に担保できず、ブラウザのレンダリングパイプラインには最大16.6msの遅延が生じることが指摘されている。そこで、イベントフローのキャプチャ相を利用してJSレベルで連続入力を即時に弾く実装を紹介し、UIより広域なインターセプトで不正な多重発火を防ぐ方法を提案している。具体的には、windowでクリックイベントをキャプチャ相に登録し、直前の入力から閾値以上の間隔を空けつつ、条件を満たす場合に stopImmediatePropagation と preventDefault で伝播を阻止する。これにより、個別コンポーネントのガードを越えた堅牢な多重発火防止が可能となり、リスナー管理の手間も削減される。

items.titleJa: Datastar入門：HTMXとAlpine.jsのいいとこ取りをした次世代ハイパーメディアフレームワーク
items.summaryJa: Datastarは、HTMXのバックエンド主導のDOM更新とAlpine.jsのフロントエンドリアクティビティを統合し、11.81 KiBの単一スクリプトで提供する軽量フレームワークです。 CDNだけで始められ、シグナルを用いた状態管理やSSEによるバックエンド主導の更新、バックエンドSDKによる多言語対応などが特徴として挙げられています。 HTMXとAlpine.jsの不足点を補う形で「バックエンドが何をどう更新するか」を決定可能とし、ビルド不要・依存関係不要で利用できます。
